findings.title: The "?" is not drawn on two of the surfaces the notes list: the sequence boards and the voice tile refuse an SVG portrait
findings.where: scripts/vault-store.mjs:601 (ROOM_IMAGE_TYPES: jpg, jpeg, png, webp, avif), :648-649; scripts/sequence.mjs:733-736 portraitOf, :970; scripts/voice-tile.mjs:725-727 voicePortrait; scripts/mask-gm.mjs:48 MASK_IMG (icons/mask-unknown.svg)
findings.what_happens: While a mask stands the actor's img is the module's SVG. Both surfaces read a portrait through safeRoomImage, which answers null for a path whose type is not a raster one. A board then draws the first letter of the student's real name in the face's place with the name under it; the voice tile falls to the next face of its list.
findings.failure_scenario: A mask stands and a board that draws the cast plays: the masked student's place shows a letter where every other student shows a picture, not the "?" the notes (v1.2.116.md 43-44) and e112/STATUS.md's table (line 110: "the sequence boards ... yes, (b)") say that surface wears.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for svg among the filter's types (none) and for another reader of the portrait on the boards (portraitOf is the one, sequence.mjs:929). E112's own item 6 agrees with this reading ("the killer's place with no picture (the masked one refused)", e112/STATUS.md 172-173) and answered it by ending the masks before the start-of-day board; the voice tile is not reached because a masked killer sits alone in a silent room (STATUS.md 108). The face stays hidden either way, so this is a wrong sentence, and the root of E118-1.

findings.title: When a GM who is not the primary ends the Eclipse, or opens the murder, the veil goes up late: the killer's token is drawn for the victim until the incident has opened and the primary has heard it
findings.where: scripts/mask-gm.mjs:552 (veilAtTheLights answers 0 off the primary), :516 (settleVeilsNow answers null off the primary), :684 (the primary settles on the incident's setting update); scripts/eclipse.mjs:399 (endEclipse asks only for a GM), :425-430, :972 (askAtTheLights awaited before openMurder at :988); scripts/murder-rules.mjs:441, :548-554
findings.what_happens: The lights' veil and the open's awaited settle both run only on the primary GM's browser. On another GM's browser endEclipse veils nobody, the Eclipse's flag goes and every token is drawn again, the lights judge there - waiting on that GM's window where the murder was not approved beforehand - and only when openMurder has written the incident does the primary's hook put the veil up. Opened from a second GM's tile in the middle of a time of day, the opening's first card and invitation likewise go out before the veil.
findings.failure_scenario: A table with two Gamemasters. A student declares a direct murder in an Eclipse. The second GM, not the primary, presses End Eclipse. On the victim's screen the killer's token is back in the room with the lights, stays there while the second GM answers the lights' window, and vanishes when the incident opens. The notes promise the killer veiled as the Eclipse ends, before its lights show anyone (v1.2.116.md 25-26), and the owner's answer (4) was from the start of the time of day the murder is declared in.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a road by which the ending GM hands the Eclipse's end or the lights to the primary: endEclipse (eclipse.mjs:399) and openMurder (murder-rules.mjs:441) ask only whether the user is a GM, and judgePendingMurders runs where endEclipse runs. Looked for a later stage that moved the veil's write: E118 changed what the veil writes, not who writes it. The notes do name the road (Known gaps, "Defaults taken, each to confirm": veiled at the open, a moment later, read off the code, not driven), so this is a stated limit rather than a hidden one; what the reading adds is that the moment includes the wait on the lights' window. Not driven by any test or scenario found.

superseded_by: E118 (line E112v, 1.2.118): the veil's mechanism - Foundry's hidden replaced by the module's mark alone; the kept-and-written-back hidden; hiddenByGm's exception for a veiled token; a GM's hide by hand during the veil is now kept
stages.grade_reasons: On 1.2.118 every promise of the stage is in the code and its core is held by behaviour tests: the veil's every road out, the Calls on the opening, the mask's picture and its give-back, the masks before the trial and the start board; the 17 registry rows are all ok in the base run's tiers 0-1 (R7405-R7408, R7520-R7527, R7540-R7543, R7560). It works in the ordinary case - one GM, or the primary ending the Eclipse. Against an 8: (1) one promise is delivered in part: with another GM ending the Eclipse or opening the murder the veil goes up late (E112-2, minor, the notes' own stated default); (2) two parts are held by reading alone - Palm applying no Call a packet names (roll-draw.mjs:1674, no test found) and the lights' call sites in endEclipse (the test calls the two functions itself); (3) the stage's first promise, as shipped in 1.2.116, had a defect a real Foundry showed at once (the veiled killer saw from the victim's token) and stands today on E118's replacement, which no canvas has seen; (4) of 5 live items one is a recorded defect, one partial, one attempted and two unread, and the ruler's three are unread. One nit (E112-1). Tier 2 and the scenarios of the base run were not joined when this was written; the tier-2 claims rest on the notes' runs.
stages.missing_to_10: The lights' veil and the open's settle reaching a table whose Eclipse a second GM ends (E112-2), with a test that ends an Eclipse holding a declared murder and reads the mark on the killer's tokens before the Eclipse's flag goes, on the primary and off it; a test that sends a Palm's packet naming an armed Call and reads none applied; a reading of LIVE-E112V-01 on a canvas (it replaces LIVE-E112-01), of LIVE-E112-02 (The Forge), -03 (the Loaded Die in Daggerheart's real window), -05 (silhouettes built for the module to hide) and LIVE-E116-01 to -03; the notes' sentence on the boards and the voice tile corrected (E112-1); E118-1 closed.

findings.title: The end-of-day board, which since F118 draws every student's portrait, plays while a mask still stands: the masked killer's place shows a letter under their real name on every player's screen
findings.where: scripts/sequence.mjs:926-934 (dayBoardOf reads portraitOf for the end board too), :733-736, :957-975, :1155-1166; scripts/clock.mjs:422-427 (the masks are ended before the write only when rolledOver); scripts/transitions.mjs:151-153, :171, :222; scripts/mask-gm.mjs:678-680; scripts/vault-store.mjs:601, :648-649
findings.what_happens: A mask writes the module's SVG to the killer's actor img and ends on the drpgTimeOfDayChanged hook, which the sync bus fires after the clock's write has landed (sync.mjs:449). On that same hook every browser builds the day's board at once (transitions.mjs:222, :168-171; sequence.mjs:1157) and reads each student's img through safeRoomImage, which refuses an SVG - so the masked student's cell is drawn as the first letter of their name with the real name under it (sequence.mjs:970-971), while the mask's end is still several awaited writes away on the primary (mask-gm.mjs:278-285: the store, each token, then the portrait). E112 closed this for the start-of-day board by ending every mask before the clock's write (clock.mjs:427 for a roll-over, eclipse.mjs:277 for the Morning Eclipse). The write that plays the end-of-day board (Evening to Night, nightFalls, clock.mjs:422) has no such call, and until 1.2.117 needed none: that board drew no cast (git show v1.2.117:scripts/sequence.mjs, dayEndBoard and dayEndElement: rows, a tally, public events, the mood). F118 made it the cast's board (55719596, which changed neither clock.mjs nor mask-gm.mjs). The board's card is then kept in each browser's notice history (sequence.mjs:1161-1164).
findings.failure_scenario: Evening. A direct murder opens (declared in the Eclipse before Evening and judged at its lights, or from the GM's tile) and the killer's opening lands on Hope or a critical, so she is behind a "?". The fight ends, nobody finds a body or enters the trial, she does not reveal herself. The GM ends the Night Eclipse (or skips it from Evening). With the table's sequences on, every player's browser plays End of day N: each student with a portrait shows it, and one living student shows a bare letter where her portrait was the evening before - the one behind the "?". The promise the notes make for this board is the cast as the table knows it; E112's own words for the same picture on the morning board were that it named the killer by elimination.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for another end of the masks before Night's write: endMask's callers are the reveal, a lost stage, the season reset, masksAtNewTimeOfDay and endMasksBeforeTheBoard, the last called from clock.mjs:153 (entering the trial), clock.mjs:427 (rolledOver only) and eclipse.mjs:277 (only when the Eclipse's patch carries dayBoard, the Morning Eclipse). Looked for a board built late enough to read the portrait given back: onClockHeard waits only for a trial's exit (transitions.mjs:169), and playDayEnd awaits one already-loaded import before it reads the cast. Looked for SVG among the image filter's types: none. Looked for a test or scenario that would have caught it: the E112 tier-2 test reads only writes carrying the start board's stamp (tests-tier2.mjs:17751-17753), F118-T1 moves Evening to Night with no mask, scenario 69 has no mask (grep: 0 hits). Looked for the case in the papers: e112/STATUS.md item 6, e112v, the 1.2.118 notes and AUDIT item 663 do not name a mask on the end board. Not run: the harness was not mine to run; a probe is E112's own test with the read moved to the write that carries nightBoard. Sized major, not blocker: no text names her the killer and the cue needs the other students to have raster portraits; sized above minor because it shows on every player's screen, in a situation any evening murder with a Hope opening reaches, and stays in the notice history.

stages.grade_reasons: One major defect, read in the source and not yet run (E118-1): F118's one board put the cast's portraits on the end-of-day board without the mask's end that E112 had put before the start board. That alone sets the grade by 11.4. Apart from it the stage is delivered as its notes word it: the veil without Foundry's hidden is held by eight tier-1 rows, two tier-2 tests and scenario 21; the log's ruling card, the second GM's frame, the Facilities words, the route charged room by room and the three smaller fixes each have a named test, and all 24 registry rows (R7561-R7567, R7700-R7707, R7740-R7744, R7790-R7793) are ok in the base run's tiers 0-1. The notes are plain about what is not there: nothing of the release ran on a real Foundry, the local gate it requires has every part not run, the sight rule is read on a stand-in class, the frames' redraw on a role change has no test, and the suite at a table is not green. Without E118-1 the grade would be 8: the main promise (the killer's own vision under the veil, the defect a real canvas showed) rests on a live check nobody has read, and several promises are held on stand-ins. Tier 2 and the scenarios of the base run were not joined when this was written.
